name: Revel
summary: Revel develops software for testing, operating, and controlling hardware in aerospace, energy, and advanced-manufacturing environments.
overview: Revel provides a modern software layer for high-consequence hardware testing and control. It announced a $150 million Series B led by Index Ventures in February 2026; the company described the round as valuing Revel at more than $1 billion.

facts.label: Latest financing
facts.note: Revel announced $150 million in Series B funding and described the milestone as more than $1 billion in value.

bull_case: A common software layer for hardware testing can become deeply embedded as aerospace and industrial customers scale increasingly complex programs.
bear_case: Hardware-sector customers have long procurement cycles, bespoke requirements, and budget sensitivity when programs are delayed.
latest_round: February 2026 Series B: $150M at a reported $1B-plus valuation
directory_notes: Public financing and operating data remain limited.

company: Revel builds software for running, testing, and controlling physical systems where reliability and safety are critical. Its initial focus included aerospace startups, while the product is designed for other advanced-manufacturing and energy use cases.

The company announced a $150 million Series B led by Index Ventures in February 2026. Revel's newsroom described the financing as a $1 billion-plus valuation milestone, though the round announcement did not state a precise valuation.
intelligence.why_it_matters: As aerospace, defense, energy, and advanced manufacturing attract capital, the software systems used to test and operate hardware can become valuable infrastructure. Revel is a private-market read-through on that tooling layer.

changed.text: Revel announced a $150M Series B and reported a valuation above $1B.

takeaways: The February 2026 Series B is the latest disclosed financing event.
Aerospace and industrial testing workflows are the core vertical opportunity.
Customer concentration and programme timing remain key risks.
